title: Investigation of the effect and mechanisms of moxa smoke in the treatment of Influenza A Virus (IAV) infection.
authors: Cao, Ting; Pan, Wenchao; Liang, Ziyao; Quan, Jingyu; Zhang, Miaona; Li, Huameng; Fan, Long; Yu, Xuhua
one_liner_zh: 该文研究艾烟对甲型流感病毒感染的抗病毒抗炎作用及机制，涉及分子对接但核心是湿实验与药理学，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Influenza, primarily caused by the Influenza A virus, is a highly contagious respiratory disease. While moxa burning is a traditional method used to reduce respiratory infections, most studies have focused on the components of moxa and air disinfection, often neglecting the pharmacological effects and mechanisms of moxa smoke. This study aimed to explore the antiviral and anti-inflammatory effects of moxa smoke in vivo, as well as the underlying mechanisms involved. Utilizing multiple databases, we identified 52 components of moxa smoke that target 384 proteins, with 92 of these potentially linked to protection against H1N1. Network analysis conducted using Cytoscape revealed 16 core targets, including PPARG and STAT3. We performed molecular docking to verify the stable binding affinities of core compounds with their corresponding targets. In vivo experiments demonstrated that moxa smoke significantly decreased the number of inflammatory cells in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), lowered the levels of H1N1 nucleoprotein (H1N1NP), and reduced the mRNA expression of cytokines with chemokines in lung tissue, including Il-6, Il-1beta, Tnf-alpha, Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl10 and Ccl2. These results suggest a reduction in lung inflammation in mice infected with the PR8 strain of the IAV. Western blot analysis indicated that moxa smoke upregulated PPARgamma and reduced phosphorylated STAT3 levels. GW9662 inhibited the reduction of recruitment of inflammatory cells by moxa smoke, but didn't inhibit the reduction of viral load after moxa smoke treatment. A four-day treatment did not cause functional injury to the lungs, kidneys, or liver of H1N1-infected mice. However, after four weeks of exposure to moxa smoke, the mice exhibited changes in organ weight and pathological damage in the lungs and kidneys. In summary, Moxa smoke suppressed influenza virus-induced inflammatory cell infiltration by upregulating PPARgamma, while simultaneously reducing viral load through PPARgamma-independent mechanisms. Short-term exposure to moxa smoke did not cause significant impairment of pulmonary, hepatic or renal function; however, prolonged exposure may result in respiratory and renal dysfunction, potentially leading to more severe adverse effects.
abstract_zh: 流感主要由甲型流感病毒引起，是一种高度传染性的呼吸道疾病。尽管艾灸燃烧是减少呼吸道感染的传统方法，但大多数研究集中于艾灸的成分和空气消毒，往往忽视了艾灸烟雾的药理效应及其机制。本研究旨在探讨艾灸烟雾在体内的抗病毒和抗炎作用，以及其涉及的潜在机制。利用多个数据库，我们鉴定了艾灸烟雾中的52种成分，这些成分靶向384种蛋白质，其中92种可能与抵抗H1N1相关。使用Cytoscape进行的网络分析揭示了16个核心靶点，包括PPARG和STAT3。我们进行了分子对接以验证核心化合物与其对应靶点之间的稳定结合亲和力。体内实验表明，艾灸烟雾显著减少了支气管肺泡灌洗液（BALF）中的炎症细胞数量，降低了H1N1核蛋白（H1N1NP）的水平，并减少了肺组织中细胞因子和趋化因子的mRNA表达，包括Il-6、Il-1beta、Tnf-alpha、Cxcl1、Cxcl2、Cxcl10和Ccl2。这些结果表明，在感染IAV PR8株的小鼠中，肺部炎症有所减轻。Western blot分析显示，艾灸烟雾上调了PPARgamma并降低了磷酸化STAT3的水平。GW9662抑制了艾灸烟雾对炎症细胞募集的减少作用，但并未抑制艾灸烟雾处理后病毒载量的降低。为期四天的治疗未对H1N1感染小鼠的肺、肾或肝功能造成损伤。然而，在暴露于艾灸烟雾四周后，小鼠表现出器官重量变化以及肺和肾脏的病理损伤。总之，艾灸烟雾通过上调PPARgamma抑制了流感病毒诱导的炎症细胞浸润，同时通过不依赖PPARgamma的机制减少了病毒载量。短期暴露于艾灸烟雾未对肺、肝或肾功能造成显著损害；然而，长期暴露可能导致呼吸和肾功能障碍，可能引发更严重的不良效应。
